prompt: Design a polished front-cover image for a book titled "How You Got Rich?". This should look like a real bookstore-ready cover, not a poster or social graphic. Portrait composition with aspect ratio 2:3. Overall tone: clean, modern, editorial nonfiction, Japanese minimalist, disciplined abstract, serious, book-cover-ready. Reserve strong, readable space for the title and author typography. If exact typography becomes unstable, prefer a clean typographic zone over garbled fake text. Include the subtitle "A Dynamic Field Book on Wealth, Business, and Method" if the typography stays clean and legible. Include the author or curator line "School of Hard Knocks / LazyingArt LLC" if the typography stays clean and legible. Visual direction: Use Japanese minimal composition: broad negative space, elegant geometric finance pathways, sparse cityline motifs, a single flowing path through abstract wealth fields, calm editorial textures, no people. Color palette: warm paper cream, matte charcoal, muted indigo, restrained vermilion accent. Avoid watermarks, mockup scenes, clutter, stock-photo cliches, distorted typography, unreadable tiny text. Front cover only. No spine. No back cover. No watermark.
